To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
open to isoclincal upright folds with N N E -striking axial planes have overprinted westerly plung ing isoclinal folds that are reclined, inclined or rare upright.

the interference patterns of the later folding were caused by variable angle of the axes and the axial planes of early folds, angular variations in the attitudes of two fold systems, spatial variations in the intensity of the later folding.

1. the early folds are upright to reclined and have NNE-stri king axial planes, 2. the late folds are upright to inclined and have WNW-stri king axial surfaces, 3. the early folds have a wide range of axial plane dips and plunge directions, and 4. the late folds have a wide variety of axial surface dips, but plunge in the same direction as the early folds.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of interference patterns produced by upright folding of varying intensity and of different orientation in a Precambrian gneiss complex in central Rajasthan, in the western part of the Indian shield.
the development of a model for the formation of the Precambrian rocks of the Amet and Lawasardargarh areas in central Rajasthan, and the interpretation of the structural and metamorphic data.

the study of the structural evolution of the Precambrian BGC of Rajasthan, India, and the development of the regional structure of the region, and the relationship of the Precambrians with the younger rocks of the region.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the early Precambrian BGC of central Rajasthan, India is a composite of two orogenic belts, one with an east-west trend and the other north-south, and that these two belts are separated from each other by a major shear zone which is a part of the Aravalli-Mewar Shear Zone.
the early folds are of the same age and that the later folds are of different ages.
the early Precambrian B. G. C. of central Rajasthan has been affected by at least three phases of deformation, each phase being characterized by a different type of fold pattern.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in the Early Precambrians of western India, the upright folding of varying intensity has overprinted the westerly plung ing isoclinal folds with NNE striking axial planes of diverse attitudes, which themselves were reclined, inclined or rarely upright.

the interference patterns of diverse shapes and sizes (from inches to miles) are caused by 1. variable angles between the axes and the axial planes of the earlier folds, 2. angular variations in the attitudes of two fold systems, 3. spatial variation in the intensity of later folding.
the early Precambrian B.G.C. between Amet and Sardargarh has been affected by two fold systems of diverse orientations and varying intensity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the folding process in the early Precambrian BGC was not a simple, straightforward, single-phase event, but was a complex and multi-phased process.
the early folds have a strong influence on the geometry of the late folds and the interference patterns.
the presence of a large-scale fold system can significantly alter the pattern and orientation of the smaller-scale folds.
